summary: Fine-tuning makes sense when you need to change a model's intrinsic behavior, style, or output format consistently, or when you must adapt to specialized domain language that prompting alone cannot reliably produce. RAG is better when the goal is injecting fresh or proprietary factual knowledge that changes over time, while prompt engineering is the cheapest first step for most tasks. Reach for fine-tuning only after prompting and RAG plateau, since it adds data-prep, training, and maintenance overhead.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when you need consistent output structure, tone, or formatting that few-shot prompting can't reliably enforce across every request.
Use it for domain adaptation where specialized vocabulary or reasoning patterns (legal, medical, code) must be baked into the model's weights.
Prefer RAG over fine-tuning when the underlying knowledge is frequently updated or must be citable, since retraining is slow and expensive.
Fine-tune to reduce latency and cost by distilling long prompts into model behavior, or for instruction/RLHF alignment on proprietary preference data.
